cards.text: Friend, meet John the Baptist, the man who's been out by the Jordan baptizing people with water (John 1:26, 28). It's the next day, and John is there again with two of his disciples. Grab your apron, baker, because this is where it all starts.
Then here comes Jesus, just walking by. John sees Him and speaks up.

cards.question: As Jesus walks by, what does John the Baptist say about Him?

answers.text: Look at the Lamb of God
Look at the Lion of Judah
Look at the Son of David

cards.question: When John's two disciples hear him call Jesus the Lamb of God, they stay right where they are with John.

cards.text: So now two guys are walking right behind Jesus, and Jesus turns and sees them following. You KNOW that moment, friend, when somebody turns around and you have to act like you were headed that way anyway.

cards.question: Jesus asks the two followers, "What do you want?" What do they ask Him back?
When the two followers answer Jesus, they call Him ___, which means Teacher.

cards.text: "Come and see," Jesus replies. No address, no directions, no pin dropped in the group chat, just COME.

cards.question: The two followers go and see where Jesus is staying, and they spend that day with Him.

cards.text: It was about the tenth hour. And one of those two followers has a name: Andrew, Simon Peter's brother.

cards.question: After his day with Jesus, who is the first person Andrew goes and finds?
Andrew tells his brother Simon what they've found. What does he say they've found?

cards.text: Messiah, which is translated as Christ. Andrew brings Simon to Jesus, and Jesus looks at him and says, "You are Simon son of John."

cards.question: Jesus tells Simon son of John he will be called by a new name. What is it?

cards.text: Cephas, which is translated as Peter. Friend, it took an ANGEL and a ride out of a junk drawer just for me to keep MY name, and Simon walks up and gets a brand new one in one sentence.
The next day, Jesus decides to set out for Galilee. And He finds a man named Philip.

cards.question: When Jesus finds Philip, He tells Philip to ___ Him.

cards.text: Philip is from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter, so somebody's hometown group chat is about to get BUSY. Then Philip goes and finds a man named Nathanael.

cards.question: Philip tells Nathanael who they've found. How does Philip describe Jesus?

answers.text: The One Moses wrote about in the Law
The One the priests chose in the temple
The One the elders sent from Jerusalem

cards.text: Then Philip says where He's from: Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph. Nathanael hears the word Nazareth, and I don't think he's sold.

cards.question: When Nathanael hears that Jesus is from Nazareth, what does he ask?

answers.text: Can anything good come from Nazareth
Where in the world is Nazareth

cards.question: Philip answers Nathanael with the same three words Jesus said to the first two followers: Come and ___.

cards.text: No debate, no slideshow, no forty-five minute speech, just come and see. And as Nathanael walks up, Jesus sees him coming and says something about him.

cards.question: As Nathanael walks up, Jesus says he is a true Israelite with no deceit in him.

cards.text: I bet Nathanael's jaw hits the FLOOR. He asks, "How do You know me?"

cards.question: Jesus tells Nathanael He saw him before Philip ever called him. Where was Nathanael?
After Jesus tells him about the fig tree, Nathanael calls Jesus the Son of God and the ___ of Israel.

cards.text: Friend, Nathanael went from doubting to ALL IN faster than my oven preheats. And Jesus says to him, "Do you believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree?"

cards.question: Jesus tells Nathanael that the fig tree is the biggest thing he will ever see.

cards.text: Not even close: Jesus says, "You will see greater things than these." Baker, the fig tree was just the TRAILER.

cards.question: Then Jesus says they will all see heaven open. What will they see ascending and descending on the Son of Man?

findings.problem: "Come and see" first appears in John 1:39, and stop 1 card 8 already quotes it in full. This card asks about the repeated line in 1:46 and even says it is "the same three words Jesus said." That gives the baker the answer, so the card tests nothing. Ask about the line only at its first appearance, or ask something else about verse 46.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 1 by a wide margin. Of its 8 choice cards, 5 are multiple choice, 2 are true or false and only 1 is fill in the blank. Cards 11, 12 and 14 are three multiple choice cards out of the last four.

rule.text: They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers share the same odd pattern ("Elijah come back" and "Moses come back"), and only the right answer is a plain title. That makes "The Messiah" stand out from the others.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: "After his day with Jesus" adds a time the text doesn't give. John 1:41 says only that Andrew "first found his brother Simon." It doesn't say this happened after the day ended.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The joke compares two different actions: Papa Dorin keeping his old name and Simon getting a new one. It also depends on a backstory detail bakers aren't told on this card: Papa Dorin asked the angel to keep his name. Without that, "it took an ANGEL ... just for me to keep MY name" doesn't click. It also makes keeping his name sound harder than it was, since in his backstory the angel simply agreed.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The same joke setups repeat across the two stops. Group chat jokes appear in stop 1 card 8 and stop 2 card 3. The "No X, no Y, no Z, just come" rhythm appears in stop 1 card 8 and again in stop 2 card 8. The second use of each feels like a formula and less funny.
findings.question: Should the docs have a rule against reusing the same joke image or structure within one walkthrough, and if so, should these cards be rewritten?
